transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-11 16:00 UTC
Duration: 49 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (Solaris Head ML Infra), Jonas (SRE), Ellen (Security), Amir (Product)

Summary:
- Diego walked through the Console's request trace playback, error grouping and root cause hints, and KV cache fallbacks.
- Customer is evaluating hosted vs private; primary concerns are PII residency, KMS integration, and reproducible request forensics.
- Agreed to run a replay benchmark and share security artifacts; follow-up scheduled for late Oct.

Topics: request trace playback, error clustering, request-level logs, KV/Prefix cache, fallback model routing, private deployment security, KMS/HSM, latency vs cost tradeoffs

00:00 Maya: hey everyone, uh, thanks for joining. i'm Maya from Redwood, i run the account.
00:18 Priya: hi thanks, i'm Priya, i'll kick us off - main goal today is to see how we can debug a user-facing failure end-to-end, like from request to tokens to fallback, um and what we need to ship to compliance.
00:30 Diego: great, we'll do a live walkthrough in the Console. i'll start with a quick look at the request inspector and then jump into trace playback for a failed batch from your sample.
00:45 Jonas: quick ask - we care about preserving the KV cache and being able to replay with the same cache state, is that possible?
01:02 Diego: yes, we have prefix and kv cache export hooks, you can snapshot KV state tied to a session id; we also simulate cache miss scenarios in playback. sometimes the transcript might show "kay vee" spelled weird, but it's the same thing.
01:22 Ellen: from security, we need to confirm audit logs and whether the playback ever sends data to Redwood hosted endpoints when running on Private.
01:33 Maya: good call, we'll show the private control plane flow and point to the audit retention settings.
01:45 Diego: switching screens — opening Console -> Request Inspector. so here you see a list of recent requests, each row has request id, model, latency, error tag. i'm going to filter to requests that returned error code 502 and high tail latency.
02:10 Amir: can you show the token-level view? we want to see where the model dropped off.
02:18 Diego: yep, clicking into a failed request... token timeline shows prefix, KV hits, attention blowups, and the generated tokens. you can scrub the timeline and replay generation in real time, or fast-forward.
02:40 Diego: note: the autogenerated diagnosis is heuristic-based — it will surface candidates like "kv cache eviction" or "kernel OOM" but it's not perfect, we recommend engineer review.
03:05 Priya: i see an item 'fallback to smaller model' — how does that decision happen?
03:12 Diego: routing policy is rule-based and cost-aware; you can set thresholds for latency SLO and if the primary model misses its concurrency budget, we fallback to pinned compatible variant. that tradeoff is explicit in the policy and visible in the trace. sometimes the transcription shows 'fal back' spelled funny.
03:40 Jonas: in the trace playback, are we able to re-inject the exact s3 payload and headers, like auth headers for a full end-to-end repro?
03:51 Diego: yes, request-replay supports payload+meta reproduction. for private deployments that replay stays inside your VPC by default — we only store pointers in the control plane.
04:10 Ellen: what about encryption? where are the logs and are they encrypted at rest with customer KMS?
04:19 Maya: we support customer-managed keys (HSM or cloud KMS). for Private we can point logs to your log collector, or keep them in Redwood with CMEK. we'll drop links to the KMS integration doc.
04:38 Diego: now i'll show error clustering — Console groups similar errors across requests using fingerprinting. you can click a cluster and see the top 10 representative requests, common stack traces, and a timeline of regressions.
05:05 Diego: example: this cluster shows rapid increase after a model rollout, the trace shows KV cache size contamination when sequence length jumped.
05:22 Priya: could you highlight how to tie that cluster back to a specific canary rollout?
05:30 Diego: each request is tagged with rollout id and model version; the playback header shows model binary hash, quantization profile, and host id. there's also a 'rollback suggestion' button that triggers a canary revert flow in Dedicated.
05:50 Amir: nice — does the Console show cost attribution per request/token?
05:55 Diego: yep, token-level cost is displayed along the timeline; when a fallback is used you'll see two cost lines — primary vs fallback.
06:20 Jonas: latency vs cost question: if we pin a model with higher throughput but higher token cost, can we route only critical traffic to it?
06:29 Diego: absolutely, routing policies can be predicate-based (header, route, user tier) so you can send high-value traffic to the high-SLA model and everything else to the cheaper fallback.
06:45 Ellen: when you do playback, are secret traces redacted? we can't have PII flying around in logs.
06:53 Diego: Console has PII redaction rules; by default sensitive fields are masked in the UI and audit logs. we also provide a scrubbed replay mode and a full replay mode for trusted infra roles.
07:10 Priya: ok can we try a real example from our sample workload? i'll point you to the request id we uploaded.
07:18 Diego: sure - searching for the id... got it. this one failed with a soft-failure at 1.2s where the model returned repeated tokens.
07:30 Diego: hitting 'Play' — you can see generation at token 34 where prefix mismatch caused a cache miss, so the model regenerated a different branch. sometimes the auto-transcribe calls it "regen" which is shorthand.
07:55 Maya: pointing out a subtlety — often customers see higher latency during cold starts; Console traces include the container spin-up time and kernel warmups.
08:10 Jonas: can we simulate cold start vs warm path in the playback?
08:18 Diego: yes, there are toggles to force cold start or to prepopulate KV cache. we'll run both to show difference.
08:35 Diego: forcing cold start now... you can see init time jumps from 80ms to 420ms and token latency shifts.
08:52 Priya: interesting, and that aligns to our issues in peak onboarding flows.
09:05 Diego: moving to request logs — the log pane includes request headers, body, model config, runtime metrics, and host-level telemetry. we also show contiguous traces so you can open the corresponding infra span in the tracing view.
09:28 Amir: how detailed are the infra spans? we have custom instrumentation in our GRPC layer.
09:35 Diego: Console supports distributed tracing via OpenTelemetry; if you send trace ids we link the request to your spans. there is occasional mismatch in names due to instrumentation, which is expected.
09:50 Ellen: for compliance, we need immutable audit trails and exportable logs for SOC audits.
09:58 Maya: we provide export APIs and can push to your archive bucket with retention rules, and retain immutable trails for configured windows.
10:12 Diego: jumping back to error analysis — the Console surfaces probable root causes and suggested remediation steps. for example, it suggested 'increase KV capacity' for this trace and shows the affected token ranges.
10:28 Priya: can we create an automation to open a ticket when a cluster spikes?
10:33 Diego: yes, alerts can be wired to PagerDuty/Slack/Jira with templated payloads that include a link to the trace and suggested runbook.
10:45 Jonas: any limitations on how long you retain full token timelines?
10:52 Maya: retention is configurable by plan; hosted has default 90 days full timeline, Dedicated and Private can extend or offload to customer storage.
11:05 Priya: about private deployments — if we run Redwood Private in our VPC, where does the control plane live?
11:15 Maya: control plane can be hosted by Redwood or run in a customer-managed control plane (air-gapped option). for the hosted control plane we use link proxies so no payload is stored in our hosted layer when configured to route audit logs to customer sink.
11:33 Ellen: KMS question again: what key lifecycle policies do you support?
11:39 Maya: rotate on schedule, disable keys, and we support HSM-backed keys via Cloud KMS or on-prem HSM. we'll include a diagram.
11:50 Diego: back to playback — i'm going to show a multi-request forensic where a downstream microservice returned a 500 and triggered a fallback cascade.
12:05 Diego: you can step through request A -> B -> C and see the propagated request-id. the Console shows correlated traces and highlights the originating latency spike.
12:28 Amir: is cross-service tracing auto-correlated or do we need to instrument?
12:35 Diego: we try to auto-correlate using headers; best practice is to instrument with OTel to get full fidelity.
12:48 Priya: we also want to test model rollbacks automatically if regression is detected. is that built in?
12:55 Diego: yes — rollback playbooks can be tied to quality monitors; if eval metrics breach thresholds, the system can trigger canary halt and rollback. the Console surfaces the suggested rollback and impact estimate.
13:18 Jonas: about request replay — how do you ensure deterministic replay given non-deterministic sampling in some models?
13:26 Diego: we seed RNGs and capture model sampling state; for non-deterministic ops we provide a 'best-effort repro' and flag variance in the playback UI.
13:42 Priya: hmm ok, that helps.
13:50 Diego: now running the 2-hour sample replay you shared earlier; i'll run it in a sandbox mode that isolates resources and measures token-level cost. starting run...
14:10 Diego: run has begun, Console gives you progress, errors per minute, and a heatmap of token consumption.
14:28 Maya: while that runs, quick note on pricing - we'll provide a sample cost model for your reported qps; but Dedicated is usually better for predictable throughput and lower per-token costs when volume is high.
14:43 Priya: we have bursty traffic — can Dedicated handle bursts without blocking?
14:50 Maya: Dedicated supports burst capacity and autoscaling policies; you can configure a burst bucket. if you need instant bursts beyond commit, hosted fallback options are available.
15:08 Jonas: any network egress costs if we ship logs to our S3 in another region?
15:15 Maya: there may be egress fees depending on your arch; for Private when logs never leave the VPC egress is not an issue.
15:28 Diego: playback results coming in — we got a small cluster of regeneration errors around minute 42 of the replay; showing cluster.
15:45 Diego: cluster shows repeated token loops tied to a specific quantization profile; looks like the quantization config caused repeated low-entropy outputs.
16:02 Priya: are quantization profiles visible in the model meta?
16:07 Diego: yes, model metadata includes quantization type, bitwidth, and kernel hints; also we show the selected kernel path for each host. sometimes the console transcriber mangles 'kernel' to 'kernal' but it's the same.
16:25 Amir: curious about developer experience — if an engineer wants to iterate on prompts, can they use the Console to edit a request and re-run locally?
16:33 Diego: there's an inline request editor with parameter tweaking, you can replay just that modified request against a chosen model/version. this is great for root-cause isolation.
16:48 Ellen: for audits, can we lock down who can run full replays that might expose PII?
16:56 Maya: yes, RBAC is per-action; you can restrict replay and see an immutable log of who ran it.
17:10 Priya: can you show the trace for the sample failing user flow that includes an external API call?
17:18 Diego: pulling it up — here's the external API call span; you can expand and see latency, status, and payload size. we also flag third-party timeouts.
17:38 Jonas: if the external API is flaky, can the Console simulate degraded responses during replay?
17:45 Diego: yes, there's fault injection: you can stub out downstream responses or add latency. we often use this to validate fallback logic.
18:03 Diego: one more feature — error annotation. engineers can annotate a trace with findings and link to a Jira, and annotations are searchable across traces.
18:20 Priya: that would help cross-team debugging.
18:33 Diego: playback finished the sandbox run — results show 0.7% error regressions, top cause: quantization profile mismatch, second: cold-start spikes during bursts.
18:50 Diego: i'll export the result summary and link it in the notes.
19:05 Maya: recap briefly — we'll share the security pack, run a 24h replay on your workload, and provide detailed cost/latency estimates.
19:20 Priya: thanks, next step for us is to sign off on the security pack and give Diego sample traces.
19:30 Ellen: we'll also schedule the KMS deep-dive after reviewing the docs.
19:40 Maya: perfect. i'll follow up with a calendar invite for the week of Oct 25 and upload the docs to the CRM record.
19:55 Jonas: quick note — competitor comparison we did showed Vertex latency higher at our seq lengths, so we're excited to see the Dedicated numbers.
20:10 Maya: great, thanks everyone.

Notes: transcription has occasional mis-hearings (e.g., 'kay-vee' for KV, 'kernal' vs kernel), filler words present. Links shared during the call: security pack (https://redwood.example.com/sec-pack/SOL-0043), replay benchmark sheet (https://sheets.example.com/replay-bench-sol-0043).

End of transcript.
